consumer_prices.reason: Interim convention under d1982 option A (2026-10-26). The donor's stored person-level bank, stock and bond assets convert once at this declaration's rate and round half-even to cents, with factor one and no ageing. The build declares a 1 April 2026 snapshot as a convention and claims no valuation date or authenticated donor lineage. S0's asset test reads this stock, S1 turns the test off and runs beside it, and the result claims no New Zealand calibration. It stays an unpublishable diagnostic under the D2 publication block.

G8-r2c activates P1: nz.earnings.map runs transport.quantile_map@2 on the TY2026 wage cuts scaled by the P1 TY2026-to-TY2027 factor, with a grouped Pareto open top, and nz.earnings.cents writes employment_income_cents half-even. No FX rate or donor factor touches wages.

rent.reason: MC4 quantile-maps rent onto the Census 2023 weekly-rent bands (C1). nz.rent.map runs transport.quantile_map@1 within each household region, on annual edges at 52 times each weekly cut. The bands hold Census 2023 levels; the C1 rent ageing ruling remains open. The MBIE bond reference P2 stays parked.

notes: The rate is the IRS 2024 yearly average for the New Zealand dollar, quoted in NZD per USD, so a donor amount is multiplied by it. Calendar-2024 money is a declared convention covering flows and asset stocks; the donor monetary basis has not been authenticated against a producing manifest. The US build's PERIOD = 2024 and the exporter's _time_period write provide model-period lineage evidence. Money normalization refuses a donor whose recorded _time_period differs from calendar 2024 (G8-w H1); this runtime check is a consistency check, not authentication. No donor file is opened to establish this declaration. Variants V1 and V2 age with their own aging_index profile (G8-w H2). public_pension_income is dropped at CREATE and is not declared.
